messages.author: 4391a11a04482aae
messages.subject: DSM Abundance response variable
parts:
Hai Eric,

Are there any limitations to the use of the abundance.est response when fitting a dsm?
I have successfully fitted some models using count as the response but each time input abundance.est as the response, R will seem to be running the model for a very long time (the most I have left running is 1.5hr) then terminate/abort the entire R session and I have to reload everything. Below is the code am using with Land cover and surface water covariates;

##Abundance as response variable
> dsm.LULC_GSM.Ab <- dsm(abundance.est ~ s(Tree_cover, k = 10) + s(Shrubland, k = 10) + s(Grassland, k = 10) + s(Cropland, k = 10) + s(Built, k = 10) + s(Bare_Spare, k = 10) + s(Water, k = 10) + s(Wetland, k = 10) + s(GSM.Freq, k = 10), detfc.hn.null, segment.data = segment.data, observation.data = obsdata, engine = "gam", method = "REML")

messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] DSM Abundance response variable
parts:
That's quite the model Chaona, with 9 predictor variables. Nevertheless, waiting for >1hr does seem excessive; however run time is a function of sample size (number of segments).

We don't commonly use estimated abundance as the response, as results should be quite similar with count as the response. Hence, I can't tell you if the run time is unusual.

Noted regarding the similar results where count or abundance is used, I just thought it would be useful to check since I have observation-level covariates.
My data has 4860 segments while the prediction grids are just over 17500.

Chaona
